cases.input: Review a completed frontend against the project's confirmed design context.
requiredBehaviors: review against PRODUCT.md DESIGN.md and the feature brief
prioritize findings with evidence and verification criteria
distinguish normative violations from preferences
forbiddenBehaviors: treat every stylistic preference as a defect

cases.input: A review finds a local pattern that would be better as a global design-system rule.
requiredBehaviors: flag the global-impact recommendation for design re-grilling
keep the review from silently changing DESIGN.md
provide the smallest useful recommendation
forbiddenBehaviors: hide global impact as a surface-only polish

cases.input: A polished-looking page uses generic AI card grids and glass effects but matches no confirmed project rule.
requiredBehaviors: call out AI-slop patterns explicitly
preserve evolutionary improvement rather than gratuitous redesign
ground findings in authority or user impact
forbiddenBehaviors: praise generic AI patterns because they look polished
redesign the whole product without evidence

cases.input: Review an app whose header uses a geometric petrol logo, whose favicon is an orange lightning bolt, and whose app icon is a violet 3D glass symbol. DESIGN.md requires a coherent brand family.
requiredBehaviors: raise a high or blocking finding for brand asset incoherence
compare motif form language and color family across logo favicon and app icon
recommend the smallest change that restores one recognizable brand family
forbiddenBehaviors: approve the assets because each looks polished independently
treat favicon and app icon as unrelated decorative files
skillAnchors: Verstöße gegen das verbindliche Brand-and-Context-Gate sind mindestens `high`

cases.input: The hero says 'Transform your workflow with AI', the CTA says 'Get Started', and feature cards say 'Powerful insights', 'Seamless integration' and 'Boost productivity' for a domain-specific product.
requiredBehaviors: raise a high finding for generic non-contextual copy
identify missing project terminology and domain specificity
recommend copy that reflects the actual project context without inventing new product strategy
forbiddenBehaviors: accept generic SaaS claims because they are clear

cases.input: DESIGN.md prioritizes rapid capture, structure from chaos and Obsidian graph handoff. The implemented hero image is only a smiling stock person with a laptop.
requiredBehaviors: raise a high finding for semantic image mismatch
verify that fewer than two prioritized project properties are communicated
recommend a key visual whose elements map to at least two project priorities
forbiddenBehaviors: approve the stock image because it creates warmth
treat imagery as decoration unrelated to project meaning
skillAnchors: mindestens zwei der in `DESIGN.md` priorisierten 2–3 Projekteigenschaften

cases.input: Review an installable PWA that has a project-specific logo and matching favicon but ships without an app icon.
requiredBehaviors: raise at least a high finding for the missing mandatory app icon
identify the brand-app-icon gate as failed
prevent an overall pass while the required asset is missing
forbiddenBehaviors: mark the app icon as optional
return pass because the rest of the interface is polished
skillAnchors: bei einer App/PWA/mobile/desktop fehlt ein konsistentes App-Icon
Der Review darf nicht mit `pass` enden

cases.input: Review an app whose logo favicon and app icon share the same simplified flame-to-node mark, whose warm focused palette is documented in DESIGN.md, whose hero visual shows capture becoming structured graph nodes, and whose copy uses the project's own terminology.
requiredBehaviors: recognize brand asset coherence
recognize color-context fit
recognize context-specific copy
recognize that the key visual communicates at least two prioritized project properties
avoid false high-severity findings for compliant brand-and-context criteria
forbiddenBehaviors: invent branding defects despite evidence of coherence

cases.input: The implementation has an ambiguous hero visual, but DESIGN.md never defines the 2–3 visual project priorities needed to judge it.
requiredBehaviors: raise a finding for the missing normative design definition
mark it requires-design-regrilling
avoid inventing the missing global visual rule during review
forbiddenBehaviors: silently decide the global key-visual concept in review
label the issue surface-only when DESIGN.md is incomplete
skillAnchors: Fehlt die dafür notwendige normative Festlegung in `DESIGN.md`
statt die Lücke mit einer eigenen Designentscheidung zu füllen
